title: InMobi Taps JPMorgan and Jefferies for $1 Billion India IPO
excerpt: India's first unicorn has appointed four investment banks to manage its upcoming public offering, seeking a valuation of up to $6 billion as it re-domiciles from Singapore.
body:
• InMobi has appointed JPMorgan, Jefferies, Kotak Mahindra Capital, and Axis Capital to manage a roughly $1 billion IPO set to begin this week.
  • The SoftBank-backed mobile advertising company is targeting a valuation of $5 billion to $6 billion for its India listing.
  • InMobi is re-domiciling from Singapore to India ahead of the offering, with founder Naveen Tewari holding about 40% of the company.
  • The IPO would mark one of the largest Indian tech listings this year and a milestone for India's first unicorn, founded in 2007.

InMobi Pte, the mobile advertising platform that became India's first unicorn, has appointed four investment banks to manage an initial public offering expected to raise about $1 billion, according to people familiar with the matter.

The company has named JPMorgan Chase & Co. and Jefferies Financial Group Inc. alongside Indian banks Kotak Mahindra Capital Co. and Axis Capital Ltd. for the IPO process, which is due to kick off later this week, the people said, declining to be identified because the information is private. Spokespeople for InMobi, JPMorgan, and Jefferies declined to comment, while Kotak and Axis did not respond to requests.

A Long Road to Public Markets

The SoftBank Group Corp.-backed firm is likely to seek a valuation of $5 billion to $6 billion, Bloomberg News reported, which would place it in the mid-range of Indian publicly traded tech companies. Earlier this year, InMobi had engaged as many as eight banks — including Motilal Oswal, IIFL Capital, BofA Securities, and UBS — for advisory evaluations before narrowing the syndicate.

InMobi is currently in the process of re-domiciling to India from Singapore for the public listing, a so-called reverse flip that has become increasingly common among Indian startups preparing for domestic IPOs. The move reflects both regulatory requirements and a strategic bet on India's deepening capital markets.

"Public listings such as InMobi's would be a boon for an Indian IPO market that has waned this year, with geopolitical turmoil derailing or delaying stock sales."

— Bloomberg News

Ownership Restructuring and Pre-IPO Moves

Ahead of the listing, InMobi has undergone significant ownership changes. SoftBank recently sold a large portion of its stake back to the company for about $250 million, though it retains a small holding. The Japanese conglomerate had first invested in InMobi in 2011, creating India's first unicorn at the time.

Harvard-educated founder Naveen Tewari, who serves as chief executive officer, is now the company's largest shareholder with about 40% of the equity. InMobi also raised $350 million in a funding round from investors including Varde, Elham, and Seatown to facilitate share buybacks from SoftBank and other private equity holders, strengthening its balance sheet ahead of the offering.

Founded in 2007, InMobi built its reputation as a challenger to Alphabet Inc. and Meta Platforms Inc. in mobile advertising. The company has since diversified into marketing, content, and commerce technologies, and has been working to shore up profitability after years of slower growth. Its enterprise engine supports mobile advertising solutions for over 30,000 brands, reaching more than 2 billion users across 150-plus markets.

What It Means for Diaspora Investors

For Indian-origin investors and NRIs tracking India's tech sector, InMobi's IPO represents a rare opportunity to access one of the country's pioneering consumer technology companies through public markets. The listing comes amid a broader wave of Indian tech IPOs — including planned offerings from Zepto, Jio Platforms, and the National Stock Exchange — that could reshape investment opportunities in India's digital economy.

The company's subsidiary Glance, an AI-powered lock-screen content platform backed by Google and Jio Platforms, has reached over 370 million users and is eyeing a separate listing after InMobi's IPO. That could present an additional investment avenue tied to India's mobile-first consumer market.

Looking Ahead

About $5 billion has been raised through Indian IPOs this year, well behind the pace of the previous two record-setting years, when proceeds topped $20 billion each, according to Bloomberg data. InMobi's billion-dollar offering could provide a significant boost to what has been a sluggish market.

The plans are not yet final and could change, the people said. But if InMobi proceeds as planned, it would cap an 18-year journey from a Bangalore startup to a publicly traded company — and mark a defining moment for India's first unicorn.
